The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 09.07.2023.
2.

The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 09.07.2023 at about 01.30 p.m., petitioner was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA- 53-EL-7689 slowly and cautiously by observing the traffic rules proceeding on Bangalore-Kolar NH-75 service Road, Tavarekere village, near Lotasas School, at that time the driver of JCB bearing Reg. No. KA-53-MJ-4084 drove in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle of petitioner.
Due to which, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of the body.

Immediately, petitioner was shifted to Sri Gaurav Orthopaedic and Surgical Hospital wherein he treated as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, food, transport and other charges.
The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident he was heal and healthy and aged about 33 years, the petitioner was working as a Farmer and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled and lost his future income.
Respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest.
3.
After service of notice, both the respondents appeared before this court and filed their respective written statements.
The respondent No.1 appear through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and also denying the rash and negligent driving of the offending JCB.

sentences.text: Further, this respondent no.1 not admitted the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle and policy was inforce as on the date of accident.
Further this respondent no.1 submits that, the petitioner was not holding valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident.

The respondent No.2 appear through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and submitted that, the petitioner was driving the two-wheeler in a rash and negligent manner and came in a wrong direction and dashed the vehicle belonging to the 2nd respondent and hence the petitioner is responsible for causing the alleged accident.

It is further submitted that, the petitioner was not having a valid driving license to drive the two-wheeler and he was not wearing helmet at the time of driving and came in wrong direction and dashed the vehicle of the respondent No.2 which was parked.
Further, both the respondents denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
The petitioner colluding with the police filed the false case.
By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.
4. On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessor framed the following issues are as under:

1 . Whether the petitioner proves that, on 09.07.2023 at about 1.30 p.m., accident took place near Lotasa School, on Bangalore-Kolar NH-75 Service Road, Tavarekere village, Hosakote Taluk, Bangalore Rural District, due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the JCB vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-J-4084 as a result the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

3 . What order or Award?
5.

In order to prove the case of the petitioner, he has got himself examined as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.16 and also examined Dr. Nagaraj B. N as PW.2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.17 and 18 and closed their side.
On the other hand, respondent No.1 examined its Legal Executive as RW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2 and respondent No.2 got examined himself as RW.2.

6. Heard arguments of both the sides and perused the materials placed on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under; Issue No.1: In the Affirmative, Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following:

:REASONS:

3 8. ISSUE No.1:

sentences.text:
The petitioner has contended that on the above said date, time and place he met with accident and sustained grievous injuries occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle.
9.
The petitioner who is injured in this accident has got examined himself as PW-1 by reiterating the averments made in the petition.
He has produced the documents at Ex.P.1 to 16.

Ex.P.1 is the FIR,
Ex.P.2 is the complaint, Ex.P.3 is the Charge-sheet, Ex.P.4 is the spot mahazar, Ex.P.5 is the Sketch,

Ex.P.6 is the IMV Report, Ex.P.7 is the Wound Certificate, Ex.P.8 and 9 are the vehicle seizer mahazar, Ex.P.10 and 11 are the List of property, Ex.P.12 is the notice u/s 133 of M. V. Act, Ex.P.13 is the Reply notice, Ex.P.14 is the discharge summary, Ex.P.15 is the medical bills, Ex.P.16 is the notarized copy of Aadhar card.

10. On going through the materials, it could be seen that on 09.07.2023 at about 01.30 p.m.,
petitioner was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-EL-7689 slowly and cautiously by observing the traffic rules proceeding on Bangalore-Kolar NH-75 service Road, Tavarekere village,
near Lotas School, at that time the driver of JCB bearing Reg. No. KA-53-MJ-4084 drove in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle of petitioner.
Due to which, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of the body.
Immediately, petitioner was shifted to Sri Gaurav Orthopaedic and Surgical Hospital wherein he treated as inpatient.
Accordingly, the Hosakote Traffic Police have registered a case in Cr.No.185/2022.

After completion of the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable U/s 279 and 338 of IPC along with section 146, 196 and 187 of M. V. Act.
11.
The negligence in common parlance means and simply failure to exercise due care, expected of a reasonable prudent person.
It is a breach of duty and negligence in law ranging from an advertence to shameful disregard of safety of others.
In most instances, it is caused or heedlessness or inadvertence, by which the negligent party is unaware of the results, which may follow from his act.
Negligence is that, a breach of duty or lack of probable care in doing something.
In short, it is want of attention and doing of something, which a prudent and reasonable man would not do.

The burden is upon the petitioner to prove that, the accident occurred due to negligent driving of the driver of JCB bearing Reg. No. KA-53-MJ-4084.
12.

As we know evidence in any Summary Proceedings, "The act of Negligence" will have to be assessed on the basis of broad preponderance of probabilities and degree of proof required is not one of beyond reasonable doubt, as it is insisted in criminal case for "The Negligent Act".
13. The certified copy of the First Information (First information statement/s complaint in common para-lace) lodged before the Hosakote Traffic Police has been marked as Ex.P.2.
On receiving the First Information, the Station House Officer chose to register a case in Crime No. 185/2023.

The said certified copy of First Information Report (F.I.R.) is marked as Ex.P.1.
14.

During the Course of examination-in-chief, he got marked Ex.P1 to 13 are the only documents,
which are to be scrutinized to arrive at conclusion- whether the accident was owing to the negligent manner of riding by the rider of offending motorcycle.

The Ex.P.4 and Ex.P.5 (spot panchanama and Lokesh vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 23 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164406816/
4 Sketch), clearly discloses the place of accident and that the police, after registering the First Information, held investigation and filed the Ex.P.3, Charge- Sheet against the rider of motorcycle U/s. 279 and 338 of IPC.
The Ex.P.6 i.e., certified copy of the IMV Report discloses that, the accident was not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle in question.

15. In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M.V.Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.
16.

sentences.text: On the other hand, respondent No.1 examined its Legal Executive as RW.1 and respondent No.2 examined himself as RW.2 and in all got marked documents at Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2.
Though the respondents have taken contention that, JCB bearing Reg. No. KA-53-MJ-4084 was at all involved in the alleged accident.
But none of the above witnesses have not disputed the accident.
On the other hand, police records clearly shows that, alleged accident is caused due to the rash and negligent act of offending vehicle.
The said documents are not at all challenged by the respondents.

17. In view of the detailed discussion held above, I am of the opinion that, the petitioner has proved negligence on the part of driver of the offending vehicle and as such the accident in question had taken place.

By relying on evidence of P.W.1 and the Police records, I am of the considered view that the accident in question took place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the JCB bearing Reg. No. KA-53-MJ-4084.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.
18. ISSUE No.2:

The petitioner in his evidence has specifically deposed that, after the accident he was shifted to Sri Gaurav Orthopedic and Surgical Hospital, wherein he was admitted as inpatient and he took treatment.
Petitioner has stated in the petition that, he is undergoing deep mental shock, severe pain and sufferings.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
19. PAIN AND SUFFERING:

In the petition as well as in his evidence PW.1 deposed that,
immediately after the accident he was shifted to Gaurav Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient from 09.07.2023 to 13.07.2023.
The petitioner has produced the discharge summary marked at Ex.P.14 wherein it is mentioned that the petitioner was admitted in the Gaurav Orthopaedic and Surgical Hospital, Kolar for 04 days.

entities.text: Gaurav Orthopaedic and Surgical Hospital, Kolar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He has produced the wound certificate marked at Ex.P.7, which reveals that, petitioner has sustained closed communited fracture lateral condyle of (rt) tibia and the doctor has opined that the injury is grievous in nature.
Hence, it is clear that during the above said period the petitioner suffered lot of pain and inconvenience.
Considering all these aspects this tribunal has granted Rs.50,000/- under the head of pain and suffering.
20. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses.
In support of his plea, he has produced 16 medical bills which are marked at Ex.P.15 to the tune of Rs.79,701/-.
Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and treatment taken by the petitioner.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.79,701/- towards medical expenses.

sentences.text: 21. LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID UP PERIOD:

The petitioner has produced Ex.P.14 Discharge summaries issued by Gaurav Orthopaedic and Surgical Hospital, Kolar, it reveals that, the petitioner took treatment from the said hospital from 09.07.2023 to 13.07.2023 i.e. for 04 days.

entities.text: Gaurav Orthopaedic and Surgical Hospital, Kolar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Hence, at least 2 months is required to recover from the accidental injuries.

It is the further contended that, the injured petitioner was a farmer and earning Rs.20,000/-
per month, in support of his income he has not produced any single document before this court.

So,
in the absence of any evidence in respect of the income of the petitioner, the petitioner might have monthly income at Rs.16,000/- as per the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka fixed notional income of the year 2023 at Rs.16,000/- per month for determination of income before Lok-Adalat for the Districts coming under the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru Bench.

entities.text: High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru Bench
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The accident is of the year is 2023.
Hence, the income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,000/-p.m. as per above decision.
Hence, 2 months is to be considered as loss of income.
Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.32,000/- under this head.
22. Towards loss of future earning capacity on account of Permanent Physical Disability-

The petitioner to prove his disability, he has produced the evidence of Dr. Nagaraj B. N in order to substantiate the same, PW.2 who has opined that, total physical disability of Right lower limb at 40% and that of whole body disability at 13%.
Admittedly, the PW.2 is not a treated doctor.

Same was admitted by the PW.2 during his cross examination, the relevant evidence of the PW.2 reads as follows :
"I have not personally treated the petitioner."
He was sworn that, petitioner has got 13% disability to the whole body but he was not issued the disability certificate.
It is quite but natural that to help the petitioner doctor will give exaggerated disability.
However, looking to the nature of the injuries it is proper to came to conclusion that there is 9% of disability to the petitioner.
23. Before proceeding on merits of the claim the age of the petitioner /injured has to be determined.
Ex.P.16 is the Aadhar Card of the petitioner, wherein his DOB is mentioned as 26.10.1989 and accident took place in the year 2023.
Accordingly, I assess his age as 33 years at the time of this accident.
As per the ruling reported in AIR 2009 SCW page-3014 between SARLA VERAMA AND OTHERS VS DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND OTHERS, the relevant multiplier applicable is '16'.

entities.text: SARLA VERAMA AND OTHERS VS DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND OTHERS
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Under this head the petitioner is entitled for an amount of Rs.2,76,480/-.

24. FOOD, CONVEYANCE, NOURISHMENT AND ATTENDANT CHARGES:
Further the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took treatment as inpatient in Gaurav Hospital, Kolar as inpatient from 09.07.2023 to 13.07.2023 i.e. for 04 days Lokesh vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 23 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164406816/
6 .

entities.text: Lokesh vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of nutritious food and attendant charges.
25. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The petitioner was aged about 33 years at the time of accident, he has sustained grievous injuries.
It shows that he found difficulty in doing day to day works.
He might have suffered lot of pain and loss of amenities and comforts in life.
Therefore, considering the age, nature of injuries and percentage of disability, Rs.20,000/- is awarded under the head of loss of future amenities and happiness.
26. TOWARDS FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES :
The petitioner has claimed towards future medical expenses.
The doctor who has been examined as PW.2 has suggested for removal of the implants and estimate of this surgery will be approximately Rs.60,000/-.
By keeping nature of the injuries sustained, as he is bound to suffer medical problems in future and cannot every time depend upon Government hospital.
Hence, under this head Rs.30,000/- is awarded.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads:
1 Pain and sufferings Rs. 50,000/- 2 Medical expenses Rs. 79,701/-
3 Loss of earnings during laid Rs. 32,000/-
up period 4 Loss of future earning Rs. 2,76,480/-
capacity 5

Nutritious food and Rs. 30,000/-
attendant charges 6 Loss of future amenities and Rs. 20,000/-
loss of happiness.
7

Future Medical Expenses Rs. 30,000/-
Total Rs. 5,18,181/-
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,18,181/- under various heads.
27. LIABILITY:
In this case as discussed in Issue No.1, accident is caused due to the rash and negligent act of offending vehicle.
In this case, respondent No.1 i.e., Insurance Company has filed written arguments contending that, the Insurance policy of offending vehicle not in-force at the time of accident.
On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 submits that, the insurance was in-force at the time of accident.
Despite, providing opportunity to the owner of the offending vehicle he failed to produce the insurance policy of his vehicle.

On the other hand, insurance company i.e.,
respondent No.1 filed copy of Insurance policy and same is marked at Ex.R.2.

On going through the said insurance copy it reveals that, the period of insurance is covered between 09.07.2023 at 04:32 Lokesh vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 23 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164406816/
7 PM and 08.07.2024 at 11:59 PM.

entities.text: Lokesh vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 23 January, 2025
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Admittedly, the accident caused on 09.07.2023 at 01:30 PM.

So,
this itself shows that, at the time of accident policy was not in- force.
At that time there is no relationship of insured and insurer.
Moreover, owner of the offending vehicle i.e., respondent No.2 has not furnished insurance policy in order to show that, at the time of accident policy was in-force.
Hence, having regard to the above facts and circumstances, this court opine that, respondent No.1 has no obligation to indemnify the owner of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, under such circumstances, it is the owner respondent No.2 is held liable to pay the compensation as awarded by the tribunal.
The liability of the insurance company is hereby exonerated from the liability.
28. INTEREST:

As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.

entities.text: Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
By relying on the aforesaid decision,
6% interest awarded to the petitioners in the present case on hand. Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative.
29. ISSUE No.3:
In view of above discussions, I proceed to pass the following:
:ORDER:
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of I. M. V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.5,18,181/- with interest @ 6%
p.a., on Rs.4,88,181/- (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 being owner of the vehicle involved in an accident is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the above compensation amount with interest thereon before Tribunal within two months from the date of this award.
The liability of the respondent No.1 insurance company to pay the compensation to the petitioner is hereby exonerated.
In the event of deposit of total compensation amount, entire amount shall be released in favour of petitioner.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon, disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.
2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated:19.08.2019.

The petitioner is hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Lokesh vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 23 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164406816/
8 Book which contains compulsorily photograph of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Adhar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission by the Tribunal.

Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner after expiry of two years period of deposit on proper verification and identification,
without waiting for further order of court.
The advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

The negligence in common parlance means and simply failure to exercise due care, expected of a reasonable prudent person.
It is a breach of duty and negligence in law ranging from an advertence to shameful disregard of safety of others.
In most instances, it is caused or heedlessness or inadvertence, by which the negligent party is unaware of the results, which may follow from his act.
Negligence is that, a breach of duty or lack of probable care in doing something.
In short, it is want of attention and doing of something, which a prudent and reasonable man would not do.
The burden is upon the petitioner to prove that, the accident occurred due to negligent driving of the driver of JCB bearing Reg. No. KA-53-MJ-4084.
12.
As we know evidence in any Summary Proceedings, "The act of Negligence" will have to be assessed on the basis of broad preponderance of probabilities and degree of proof required is not one of beyond reasonable doubt, as it is insisted in criminal case for "The Negligent Act".
15. In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M.V.Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.
16.
Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and treatment taken by the petitioner.
Hence, 2 months is to be considered as loss of income.
Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.32,000/- under this head.
22. Towards loss of future earning capacity on account of Permanent Physical Disability-
He was sworn that, petitioner has got 13% disability to the whole body but he was not issued the disability certificate.
It is quite but natural that to help the petitioner doctor will give exaggerated disability.
However, looking to the nature of the injuries it is proper to came to conclusion that there is 9% of disability to the petitioner.
23. Before proceeding on merits of the claim the age of the petitioner /injured has to be determined.
So,
this itself shows that, at the time of accident policy was not in- force.
At that time there is no relationship of insured and insurer.
Moreover, owner of the offending vehicle i.e., respondent No.2 has not furnished insurance policy in order to show that, at the time of accident policy was in-force.
Hence, having regard to the above facts and circumstances, this court opine that, respondent No.1 has no obligation to indemnify the owner of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, under such circumstances, it is the owner respondent No.2 is held liable to pay the compensation as awarded by the tribunal.
